counter_evidence:
Most of the claim's specific numbers and words are contradicted by the design's own text and by primary docs.

(1) "Output capped at 2,000 characters" is wrong. In KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md, line 278 says "shown: at most one lead and one candidate ... each a card of ≤ 2,000 characters", and adds that "do-not-apply entries whose action or ident handles match are shown as a separate warning line even with no error text". Line 406 says `ks lookup` "prints `KS miss|candidate|lead <lookup-id>` on the first line ..., then at most two cards". So the real bound is a header line, plus 2 × 2,000 characters, plus warning lines: more than 4,000 characters. A miss can also print warning lines, so it is not always one line. Line 378 ("one lead card and one candidate card, 2,000 characters") reads ambiguously against line 278.

(2) "A phase in which nothing hard happens costs about zero" is contradicted by the design's own routine. §7.6 (line 442) makes every code phase run `ks lookup --files ... --action ...` at its first commit, and `ks scan --at origin/main` plus `ks sync` at phase close, and the closing message must report the two counts. Line 319 says scan "re-runs every validated declarative probe at origin/main", so its cost grows with the corpus. §7.7 (line 450) itself prices this at about 0.6k + 0.4k tokens and under 15 s per phase. That is three fixed tool turns per phase, not zero.

(3) The token arithmetic leaves out how the API bills. The pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) shows that each request re-sends the conversation history, reading the cached prefix at 0.1x base input (0.05x on Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1). Output is 5x input ($50 vs $10 per MTok on Fable 5.1). So the extra cost of one Bash call is mostly the caller's context re-read, not the output. Example: Fable at 120k context × $0.25/MTok ≈ $0.03, about 3k base-input-equivalent tokens, before the output is counted. The same page also says: "Claude 4.7 and later models ... use a newer tokenizer ... approximately 30% more tokens for the same text." The project's own ratio is CLAUDE.md 29,605 bytes ≈ 7.5k tokens (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md:90 @3415b5e), about 3.95 chars per token. At that ratio one 2,000-character card is about 500 tokens; with the newer tokenizer about 650. Two cards come to about 1.3k tokens or more, and more again for cards dense with hashes and paths.

(4) "One Bash call" holds only for a bare miss.
- **Input:** §7.1 takes `--text @err.txt` and names no stdin or capture path. In the model case ("before retrying a failed build or deploy", §7.2), the error text exists only in the agent's context. The agent must either re-emit it as output tokens (5x price) through a Write call or a heredoc, or re-run the build.
- **Hit path:** a lead adds `ks verify`, `ks show` (up to 6,000 characters per section) and `ks outcome`. §7.2 has the session "dispatch a cheap agent to `ks verify`", and every subagent pays the fixed overhead of CLAUDE.md ≈ 7.5k tokens plus the CONTEXT block (ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN:90,583). That contradicts §7.7's "1–1.5k tokens".
- **Miss path:** §7.2 adds `ks claim` on a miss.

(5) "Nothing is injected into any agent's context" is false by the design's own text. §7.6 says the session "passes a `candidate` into the brief as an unverified prior", and §7.2 puts the lookup id and dead ends into the Opus brief. Warnings are copied into the draft PR body, which every resuming session and the PR reviewer read. That is pushed context, which is exactly the mode M-02.28 (experience-following) and M-02.30 (lexically close wrong-action memories harm) warn about.

(6) The standing cost is larger than stated.
- **§0 text:** the proposed §0 text measures 260 words / 1,569 chars (line 442) plus 29 words / 185 chars (Routing sentence, line 444) = 289 words / 1,754 chars, not about 150 words. SHIP-PLAN §0 is read by the main session at phase start and re-read on resume (ship plan v8 §0 Resume bullet), so it stays in that session's context and is re-billed at the cache rate on every later turn.
- **Pointer and reviewer sentence:** line 479 adds a MEMORY.md pointer line, which loads in every main session (M02-01), and a reviewer sentence in every PR brief.
- **Skill listing:** the skills docs say "Every skill in the skill listing adds to your context on every turn". This workflow subagent's own context carries the skill listing, so the per-turn cost is multiplied across every agent in every workflow.
- **Citation:** the claim cites E-10.F17 for the skill figure, but F17 is about MCP tool search. The skill facts are E-10.F19 and M02-04.

(7) The skills docs ("Skill descriptions are cut short") say the listing budget "scales at 1% of the model's context window", and on overflow Claude Code "drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least". A pull-only store's skill is rarely invoked by design, so it is the first description dropped. Its standing cost can fall to the name alone, and its trigger with it.
trace:
What survives, with the path to it:
- **No hook:** design line 414 says "There is no hook: the store is pull-only and injects nothing". §7.1 shows every verb is agent-invoked.
- **Skill cost:** the skill contributes only its listing entry. Description plus when_to_use is truncated at 1,536 characters and the body loads on invoke (M02-04, ON_PAGE in recheck-M-02; skills docs: "combined description and when_to_use text is truncated at 1,536 characters").
- **Bash access:** Bash is inherited by every subagent with no configuration (E-10.F16).
- **Output headroom:** Bash read-back is 30k characters (E-10.F18), so a few-kB card stays far below truncation.
- **Runtime:** `node:sqlite` on this box is quiet. It printed `v24.22.1 3.53.4` with no ExperimentalWarning on stderr, so a miss really can be one line when no warning matches.
- **Dollars:** pricing per the pricing page puts these fixed costs at cents per phase.

So the order of magnitude ("small, bounded, pull-only at the store boundary") holds. The specific bounds, the "about zero" and "nothing injected" wording, and the one-call/2,000-character figures do not.
narrowed_claim:
The store has no hook, and its standing cost is small but not zero:
- **Skill listing:** one entry, at most 1,536 characters of description plus when_to_use, about 400–650 tokens. It is present on every turn of every main session and every subagent that has the Skill tool. It is the first description dropped when the listing exceeds its budget of 1% of the context window.
- **Main session:** about 290 words / 1.75k characters of SHIP-PLAN §0 text, held for the rest of the phase, plus one MEMORY.md pointer line.
- **PR reviewers:** one Routing sentence in every reviewer brief.

A phase in which nothing hard happens pays three fixed `ks` tool turns: the first-commit lookup, `scan` and `sync`. Each turn costs the caller's context re-read at the cache-hit rate, plus about 1k tokens of output in all. That is cents, not zero.

A miss is one Bash call and one line, unless a do-not-apply warning matches. Its output is bounded at a header plus two cards of at most 2,000 characters each plus warning lines, about 4–4.5k characters (about 1.3k+ tokens on the post-4.7 tokenizer). The raw error text has to reach the CLI as a file, and before a retry that means re-emitting it as output tokens. A lead adds verify, show and outcome calls and, per §7.2, a dispatched subagent with about 7.5k tokens of CLAUDE.md overhead.

"Nothing is injected" holds only if the design drops the step of forwarding candidates into escalation briefs.
what_would_settle_it:
These measurements would pin the remaining numbers:
- **Card cost:** run the token counting endpoint on a sample two-card lookup output and a 1,536-character skill description, using the models the program uses (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5).
- **Listing survival:** run `/context` (Skills row) or `/doctor` in a Haiku/Sonnet workflow subagent after the skill is added, to see whether the ks description survives the listing budget.
- **Real per-lookup cost:** in the KS-5 prospective log, record `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` and `output_tokens` for the turn that runs `ks lookup` and for the turn that produced its input file, not only the size of the CLI's output.
design_consequence:
The design should change in seven places:
1. **Output cap:** state the true lookup bound (header + 2 × 2,000 + warning lines) or make the CLI enforce a single total-bytes cap, which E-10.F18 recommends. Reconcile lines 278, 378 and 406.
2. **Error input:** add `--text -` (stdin) and/or a capture convention, so a pre-retry lookup never re-emits the error as output tokens and never re-runs a build. Either the skill/§0 routine runs gated commands as `... 2>&1 | tee <scratchpad>/last.err`, or the CLI gets a `ks lookup --log <file>` option.
3. **Fixed turns:** cut the per-phase turns. Chain the first-commit lookup into the commit's Bash call, and merge `scan` + `sync` into one `ks close` verb that prints the two counts.
4. **§7.7 estimates:** re-state them as (caller context × cache-hit rate) + output + subagent overhead. Revise the "1–1.5k tokens" for a step-zero lookup that dispatches a verifier subagent.
5. **Pull-only:** make it true. Pass only the lookup id into escalation briefs, so the receiving Opus agent pulls the card itself under the same gate. Otherwise drop the "nothing is injected" wording from §0 rule 1 and §7.1.
6. **§0 accounting:** correct the length to about 290 words and list the MEMORY.md pointer and the reviewer Routing sentence as standing costs.
7. **Trigger:** do not rely on the skill description to trigger lookups. The listing drops the least-invoked descriptions first, so the trigger must live in the §0 sentence and the briefs, and KS-5 should check that the description survives in subagents.

Also fix the register citation: E-10.F17 → E-10.F19 / M02-04.
